fact: The shared corner of two figures — the head of Andromeda and a corner of Pegasus's Great Square.
bio: Alpheratz (Alpha Andromedae) is a blue-white star about 97 light-years away with an unusual mercury-manganese chemical peculiarity. It marks the head of Andromeda while also serving as the north-eastern corner of the Great Square of Pegasus.
cultural: The name derives from the Arabic for 'the navel of the mare', from a time when the star was counted as part of Pegasus. It bridges the myth of the chained princess Andromeda and the winged horse beside her.
